confirmed.title: Take-all imputation (Stage 3) fills availability-masked lags, which are coded 0, so about half of take-all nonrespondents are imputed as zero
confirmed.failure_scenario: build_population.apply_availability (lines 117-121) sets lag_employees, lag_contrib, lag_prog_rev and lag_salaries to 0.0 whenever the t-1 return was not submitted by D. It also replaces lag_revenue and lag_expenses with BMF revenue. LAST_CYCLE (stage34_ne.py:31-36) and last_cycle_matrix (:55-59) feed exactly these columns into ta_values (:71-76). The protocol's NTEE10 trend factor and its TA-hist-aux fallback for a missing own value are not implemented. In TA-late, 179 of 206 take-all units are nonrespondents and 47% of them have avail_t1=0. Checked on the population, the imputed take-all part biases the total by: employees -19.9%, salaries -31.6%, prog_rev -35.3%, contrib -13.0%, revenue -9.1%, expenses -7.9%. In TA-follow the same biases are -2% to -3.6%. The take-some weighting-class NR bias that Stage 3 is meant to study is only -5% to -7% (contrib +1%). run_cell adds this same T_ta to every spec, including FULLRESP_GREG. So for contrib, prog_rev and all of R_SET, RB, coverage and BRF = 1-abs(RB_text)/abs(RB_ref) are dominated by the shared take-all error, and BRF is pushed toward 0 whatever the take-some method does. In TA-follow, the random take-all response error also adds variance that v ignores.
confirmed.suggested_fix: For certainty units, impute from the unit's unmasked previous-cycle survey value (the oracle_lag_* / pre-availability t-1 amounts). Fall back to TA-hist-aux (lag_expenses x ratio among responding take-all units) only when that value is missing. Apply the NTEE10 trend ratio as §7.2 specifies. Report RB on the take-some part separately so BRF is not mixed with take-all imputation error.

verdict.evidence:
I could not refute this. I reproduced it on the real population, single-threaded and with the design only. That means production_design(pop, 1000) and resp = days_to_file_t <= 300 — the same inputs stage34_ne.nr uses.

- **The zeros come from the availability mask.** ne_pop_v2.parquet has avail_t1=0 for 1,667 units. In build_population.py:117-121, apply_availability sets lag_employees, lag_contrib, lag_prog_rev and lag_salaries to 0.0 for those units. It also sets lag_revenue and lag_expenses to bmf_revenue_amt. LAST_CYCLE (stage34_ne.py:31-36) feeds these masked columns into ta_values (:71-76), which adds L[ta_idx[~rr]].sum(0).
- **Counts match the finding.** There are 206 take-all units. In TA-late, 179 are nonrespondents, and 84 of those have avail_t1=0. For all 84, lag_employees, lag_contrib, lag_prog_rev and lag_salaries are exactly 0 (min = max = 0).
- **These units do have a last-cycle return.** All 84 have a real TY2022 return. submitted_on_t1 is never NaT; it falls between 2024-07-12 and 2024-10-01, so after D but before cycle-t estimation. In parsed/ne_2022.parquet, their employees_p1 sums to 313,106, against y_employees 318,727. The code imputes 0 for them.
- **The mask is applied inconsistently.** The oracle_lag_* columns used for gov_grants, fundraising, officer_comp and volunteers are not masked. Only the register lags are.
- **Shift in TA-late, as a share of the total.** The overall shifts match the finding: revenue -9.1%, expenses -7.9%, employees -19.9%, salaries -31.6%, contrib -13.0%, prog_rev -35.3%. The 84 masked units cause -4.9%, -4.8%, -19.4%, -29.7%, -6.6% and -33.1% of that.
- **With the unmasked TY2022 values swapped in.** The shifts fall to -6.2%, -5.3%, -0.9%, -4.1%, -6.2% and -5.1%. What remains comes from the missing NTEE10 trend factor, which the protocol's TA-hist-own includes (§7.2, protocol line 712).
- **This contradicts the protocol.** Line 58 says certainty units always have a last-cycle value. Line 713 says to use the TA-hist-aux fallback when the own value is missing. Neither is implemented.
- **Every spec gets the same error.** run_cell (mc.py:419) adds the same T_ta to every spec.
- **Effect on S6.** notebooks/04_protocol_nonresponse_and_sae.py:91 computes BRF = 1 - |rb_text|/|rb_SQ| on the total RB. For contrib (one of the 5 S6 variables), both RBs carry the shared take-all shift: about -13% in TA-late, half of it from the masking. That pushes contrib's BRF toward 0 and its coverage toward 0 whatever the take-some method does.
- **Effect on other outputs.** The RB and coverage reported for employees, salaries and prog_rev in Stage 3 are dominated by the zero imputation.
- **S6 variables not affected.** gov_grants (-0.4%), fundraising (-2.1%) and volunteers (clipped, about 0%) use unmasked oracle lags, and lobbying uses the TY2022 binaries. So the masking hits only contrib among the 5. Whether S6 flips overall depends on the other four, but the Stage-3 contrib and R_SET results are invalid as computed.

1. Impute take-all nonrespondents from their unmasked own TY2022 values. In stage34_ne.setup, which already reads parsed/ne_2022.parquet as p22, add:

   for y, c in {"y_revenue": "revenue_cy", "y_expenses": "expenses_cy", "y_employees": "employees_p1", "y_salaries": "salaries_cy", "y_contrib": "contrib_cy", "y_prog_rev": "prog_rev_cy"}.items():
       pop[f"cyc_{y}"] = pd.to_numeric(p22[c].reindex(pop.ein), errors="coerce").to_numpy()

   Then point LAST_CYCLE at these cyc_* columns. An alternative is to keep a copy of each lag in apply_availability before masking.
2. Where the own value is truly missing (NaN), use TA-hist-aux: frame lag_expenses times the ratio of y to lag among responding take-all units.
3. Apply the §7.2 NTEE10 trend factor among responding take-all units in each replicate: y_imp = y_{t-1} * sum_r y_t / sum_r y_{t-1}. In TA-follow, rr changes every replicate, so the factor changes too.
4. Also report RB and BRF on the take-some part, i.e. est - T_ta_used versus truth_ts. Then S6 BRF is not mixed with take-all imputation error.

confirmed.title: Propensity (ps) adjustment is fitted in-sample on about 450 standardized columns, not cross-fitted; the propensities are mostly overfit noise
confirmed.failure_scenario: _nr_weights fits LogisticRegression(C=1) on the full take-some sample. It then predicts the same respondents, although protocol §7.2 says propensities are cross-fitted on the sample. Every column is z-scored, including rare BMF-code dummies, so a rare dummy gets scale 1/sd≈30 and is effectively unpenalized. On two replicates of the real cell, FC@F1p gave in-sample AUC 0.900/0.879 against 5-fold cross-fitted AUC 0.584/0.567. FC@F1p+Estar gave 0.908/0.886 against 0.588/0.562. The Kish factor 1+CV² of the 1/p adjustment was 6.0-7.0 in-sample against about 3.6-3.9 cross-fitted. NR_ps_frame_MCAL and NR_ps_text_MCAL therefore carry large weight noise from in-sample overfitting, which grows with the number of columns. The text-vs-frame propensity comparison and its BRF/RE reflect overfitting, not response information.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Cross-fit p_hat with the shared fold vector (predict each fold from a model fitted on the other folds). Keep categorical dummies on the raw scale, or use a penalty tuned by CV (e.g. LogisticRegressionCV on log-loss). Log the Kish factor and AUC as §7.2 requires.

verdict.evidence:
I could not refute this finding. One part is wrong: cross-fitting alone does not fix it. The real cause is the penalty, and the suggested fix has to change.

What the code does (src/mc.py lines 366-372): `_nr_weights` z-scores the columns of `cell.mats[ps_F]`, fits `LogisticRegression(C=1)` on all sampled take-some units, and predicts the same respondents. Protocol §7.2 (notes/benchmark-protocol.md line 717) says "propensities cross-fitted on the sample", and deviations.md says nothing about propensities. The §7.2 diagnostics (Kish factor, AUC of p̂ with and without text, line 743-744) are not computed anywhere. The affected specs are `NR_ps_frame_MCAL_bmfmax@F1p` and `NR_ps_text_MCAL_bmfmax@F1p+Estar` (stage34_ne.py lines 84-85), plus experiments.py lines 160-166. Stage 3 has not been run yet: results/stage34_ne holds only SAE output.

Checks, single-threaded, on the real cell (SEED=20261023, n=1000, NR-LATE, 794 take-some units in the sample, about 425 respondents):

1. Matrix size. FC@F1p has 453 columns and FC@F1p+Estar has 469.

2. AUC and Kish factor, replicates 0 and 1. AUC is design-weighted. The Kish factor is 1+CV² of 1/p over respondents.

| Matrix | AUC in-sample | AUC 5-fold cross-fitted | Kish in-sample | Kish cross-fitted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FC@F1p | 0.976 / 0.958 | 0.613 / 0.525 | 7.03 / 6.02 | 3.97 / 3.64 |
| FC@F1p+Estar | 0.980 / 0.965 | 0.605 / 0.502 | 6.15 / 6.43 | 3.82 / 3.34 |

These Kish factors match the reviewer's numbers.

3. Out-of-sample log-loss. At C=1 the cross-fitted log-loss is 1.52 and 1.76. An intercept-only model scores about 0.69, so the C=1 propensities predict worse than no model at all; they are noise. The C=1 penalty is effectively none here: a rare dummy z-scored with sd≈0.035 has its raw-scale penalty cut by a factor of about 800.

4. Penalty sweep (cross-fitted log-loss / Kish):

| C | Replicate 0 | Replicate 1 |
|---|---|---|
| 0.01 | 0.706 / 1.73 | 0.794 / 1.37 |
| 0.003 | 0.659 / 1.08 | 0.715 / 1.06 |

Cross-fitted AUC stays about 0.51-0.63 at every C. There is little real response signal in the frame.

5. Effect on the estimates. I ran a 40-replicate Monte Carlo with `run_cell` and a patched `_nr_weights`, comparing MCAL_bmfmax@F1p under rhg, in-sample ps (the current code), and cross-fitted ps with C=1. Relative RMSE in % (rhg / ps in-sample / ps cross-fitted):

| y | rhg | ps in-sample | ps cross-fitted |
|---|---|---|---|
| volunteers_cap10k | 22.0 | 44.3 | 37.1 |
| officer_comp | 22.7 | 32.3 | 25.3 |
| gov_grants | 21.7 | 25.3 | 30.5 |
| grants_to_indiv | 16.0 | 20.3 | 31.1 |
| foreign_activities | 25.0 | 28.9 | 46.6 |

The standard deviation of the paired difference (ps in-sample minus rhg) is 14-33 percentage points on several H targets. Mean bias stays close to rhg. So the ps adjustment adds noise, not a bias correction.

So the NR_ps arms, and any text-vs-frame propensity comparison, BRF or RRMSE ratio built on them (S6), are driven by noise from overfitting. The in-sample AUC reported under §7.2 would be about 0.97 and mean nothing.

Severity: this is Stage 3 / secondary claim S6. The Stage-2 primary gates are not affected, and the NR_ps arms are not in the Stage-1 reference set.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In `_nr_weights` (src/mc.py lines 366-372), make two changes together:

1. **Tune the penalty first.** Choose C on the shared fold vector by out-of-fold weighted log-loss, for example `LogisticRegressionCV(Cs=np.logspace(-4, 0, 9), cv=PredefinedSplit(folds), scoring='neg_log_loss')` fitted with weights d/mean(d). Alternatively, keep 0/1 dummies on the raw scale and z-score only the continuous columns. On this cell the chosen C comes out around 0.003-0.01, and the Kish factor drops to about 1.1-1.7.

2. **Then cross-fit, as protocol §7.2 requires.** Use `folds = cell.fold_of[cell.ts_index[s_ts]]`, and set `p[folds==f]` from a model fitted on `folds!=f` with the chosen C. Keep the 0.02 clip and the within-stratum rescaling.

Cross-fitting alone at C=1 is not enough: it raised RMSE on most y in the 40-replicate check.

Also record, per replicate, the cross-fitted AUC of p̂, the Kish factor 1+CV²(1/p̂) and the clip-hit count, as §7.2 requires.

confirmed.title: v_R (_var_counts) ignores the within-stratum variation of the ps weights, so the variance of the NR_ps arms is wrong by large factors
confirmed.failure_scenario: For nr_adj='ps', the respondent weights dr_k vary within a stratum as 1/p_k (Kish about 6). Yet _var_counts computes sum_h N_h^2(1-r_h/N_h) s^2_h(e)/r_h on unweighted residuals, which is only correct for equal weights N_h/r_h, i.e. RHG. On real-cell replicates, the ratio of the variance with g-weighted residuals (e_k * dr_k/mean_h(dr)) to v_R for NR_ps_text_MCAL_bmfmax@F1p+Estar was [0.88, 0.71, 0.91, 0.45, 1.34, 0.49] in rep 0. In rep 1 it was [1.84, 6.78, 1.31, 0.78, 1.05, 7.69] for gov_grants, contrib, prog_rev, fundraising, officer_comp and revenue. For RHG arms it was exactly 1. Coverage and var-RB of every propensity arm are therefore meaningless, with a 7x understatement for contrib and revenue in some replicates. Protocol §4.7 requires v_R,B for propensity estimators, and no deviation is logged.
confirmed.suggested_fix: For non-RHG adjustments, use at least the weighted linearization: v on z_k = (dr_k / (N_h/r_h)) * e_k within strata. Preferably implement v_R,B (a bootstrap that refits the propensity and outcome models), or log a deviation and exclude ps-arm coverage from Stage-3 claims.

verdict.evidence:
I could not refute the finding. The mechanism is real, but it is the smaller part of a larger defect.

1) Code. In mc.py:384-394, `_var_counts` computes sum_h N_h^2 (1 - r_h/N_h) s^2_h(E)/r_h on residuals E with no weights. `run_cell` (mc.py:427) calls it for every `nr` arm. For `nr_adj='ps'`, `_nr_weights` (mc.py:366-381) sets dr_k proportional to 1/p_k and then rescales within strata, so dr varies inside a stratum. Within-stratum Kish over 300 replicates: median about 1.1, worst stratum 4-11, mean 7.2. The residuals from `greg_total` / `_calibrate_each` carry no weight. The formula is only right when dr = N_h/r_h within each stratum (RHG).

2) Reproduced. I ran the real spec `NR_ps_text_MCAL_bmfmax@F1p+Estar` from stage34_ne.py (SEED 20261023, single-threaded, scratchpad script ps_var_mcal.py). The ratio of dr-weighted to unweighted variance matches the reported values exactly: rep 0 gives 0.88/0.71/0.91/0.45/1.34/0.49 and rep 1 gives 1.84/6.78/1.31/0.78/1.05/7.69. Over 200 replicates, mean(v_dr-weighted)/mean(v_R) for the ps arm is:
- contrib 1.31, revenue 1.47, expenses 1.39, employees 1.96, salaries 1.99, officer_comp 2.92, gov_grants 1.19, binaries 1.06-1.25.
- RHG arm: exactly 1.

Weighting therefore moves ps-arm variance and coverage materially. Coverage centred at the Monte Carlo mean goes from 31.0% to 40.5% for officer_comp, 82.5% to 87.0% for lobbying, and 57.5% to 61.0% for contrib.

3) Bigger issue. The finding implies the RHG arms are valid. They are not. Against the Monte Carlo variance (200 replicates), v_R has relative bias of:
- -74% to -96% on every continuous y for `NR_rhg_MCAL_bmfmax@F1p+Estar` (coverage 37-68%);
- about the same for the ps arm (-75% to -95%);
- still -67% to -90% for the ps arm after the reviewer's dr-weighted fix.

Controls look fine: v_R for `NR_rhg_HT` is within ±13%, and full-response GREG v_L is -3% to -13% (-33% for fundraising). The cause is that under nonresponse the respondent-weighted X totals miss T_X, so the calibration g-weights are far from 1: in the size_cat GREG analog, g_k ran from about -12.7 to 72. The (T_X - X̂_r)'(B̂ - B) term then becomes first order and residual-only linearization drops it. With g-weighted residuals z = dr·g·e, the GREG analog improves to -42% to -60% (RHG) and -53% to -73% (ps). That is still invalid.

4) Protocol. §4.7 lists v_R,B ("re-estimates propensity and outcome models in every replicate") for propensity and DR arms as [CODE]. It is not implemented. D-11 covers only v_B/v_g for single-weight arms, and no deviation covers v_R,B. Stage 3 S6 uses a coverage gap of at least -2 pp, and §741 reports coverage with v_R,B for propensity arms. Under-weighting inflates the ps arm's coverage gap against an RHG comparator by up to about 10 pp (officer_comp 31% vs 43%; contrib 57.5% vs 68.5%). Every NR calibration arm's coverage and var-RB is also invalid on its own terms. Stage 2 gates are not affected.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Weighting the residuals by dr is necessary but not enough, and the fix has to cover every NR calibration arm, RHG included, not only ps.

(a) Return per-target final weights from `_estimate` for NR arms. Compute v on z_k = w_k·e_k, where w_k = dr_k·g_k and g_k = 1 + (T_X − Σ_r dr x)'(Σ_r dr x x')^{-1} x_k. In `_calibrate_each`, x is [X_base, m_j] for each target j. Use v = Σ_h r_h (1 − f_h) s²_h(z) (the v_g form). With this, the FPC should use n_h/N_h.

(b) Because v_g is still -40% to -70% here, implement the protocol's v_R,B as primary for NR arms:
- resample the take-some sample within strata;
- rerun `_nr_weights` (refitting the propensity) and `_estimate` in each bootstrap replicate;
- use the bootstrap variance.

Until (b) exists, log a deviation and withhold all Stage-3 coverage, var-RB and S6 coverage-gap claims (RHG and ps alike). Report only bias, BRF and RRMSE, which come from the Monte Carlo distribution.

confirmed.title: D-6 (clip after averaging fold coefficients) biases the MCAL population total of m_hat downward, more for the text arm
confirmed.failure_scenario: The sample-side calibration variable is the clipped prediction of one fold model, so E[sum_s d m_cf] ≈ sum_U mean_f clip(m_f). The population constraint uses sum_U clip(mean_f m_f). For zero-inflated ratios the lower clip at lo=0 binds, and max(0,.) is convex, so the constraint is always too small. Recomputing on four real-cell replicates, (t_D6 - t_protocol)/SE was always <= 0: gov_grants -0.034 to -0.089 (twin) and -0.023 to -0.157 (text); fundraising up to -0.10; contrib up to -0.08. With R=2000 the MC SE of RB is about 0.022 SE, so a bias of about -0.05 to -0.1 SE is 2-4 MC SE. It is not 'negligible' as D-6 states, and it is a one-sided bias that cross-fitting was meant to avoid. The effect on RE is small (well under 1% on gov_grants), so it should not flip P1. It does, however, threaten an RB-based validity criterion (G4: abs(RB) <= 0.1 RRMSE or within 2 MC SE).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Compute sumM as the mean over folds of clip(b0_f + F Bx_f) (the protocol's definition). It costs about 5 extra (N_ts x p) products per spec, or can be done only for columns where the clip binds. Alternatively, correct the D-6 entry with the measured effect.

verdict.evidence:
The finding holds, but it is minor. Its claim that this threatens G4 is overstated.

**The cause.** In src/mc.py:266-275 (model_predict), the population total is built from one model whose coefficients are the average of the 5 fold models. Its prediction is clipped once: `P = np.clip(b0m + F @ Bxm, lo, hi)`. The sample-side column M is different: for each sampled unit it is the clipped prediction of that unit's own out-of-fold model. In expectation, the HT sum of M matches the average over fold models of the clipped predictions (the protocol's m̄), not the clip of the averaged model. Clipping at the lower bound is convex, and for zero-inflated ratios that bound is about 0. So clip(mean) <= mean(clip), and the model-calibration constraint total comes out too small.

**Why the shift is exact.** For GREG, t_D6 - t_prot = beta_m * (sumM_D6 - sumM_prot) on every sample, because beta_m does not depend on the constraint totals. The shift is therefore a deterministic, one-sided offset, not noise.

**Check run.** Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-hananather/61c19d0b-7d5d-50f6-9821-a76e0ea08cdb/scratchpad/d6check.py. It is single-threaded and uses the same SEED, draws and shared grouped folds as run_cell, with only size_cat@F1p, FC@F1p and FC@F1p+Estar built. Over replicates 0-3 it recomputed the population total both ways and the GREG estimate on each. Values are the mean shift (t_D6 - t_prot) / SE, where SE = sqrt(v_L):

| Target | Text arm: mean (range) | Twin: mean (range) |
|---|---|---|
| gov_grants | -0.084 (-0.157 to -0.023) | -0.053 (-0.089 to -0.034) |
| fundraising | -0.061 | -0.062 |
| contrib | -0.041 | -0.022 |
| volunteers | -0.018 | -0.005 |

- Binaries are unaffected (no clip).
- employees has a small positive shift (+0.008), where the upper clip (concave) binds instead.
- The constraint total itself is 0.4-2% too low for gov_grants.

These numbers reproduce the reviewer's figures. At R=2000 the MC SE of the bias is about 0.022 SE, so a bias of -0.05 to -0.08 SE is roughly 2-4 MC SE. It will be visible in the reported RB. The D-6 entry in prereg/deviations.md calls it "Negligible through clipping", which is not accurate for the amounts.

**Effect on verdicts.** It does not change any verdict:
- **RE:** MSE goes up by about delta^2, roughly 0.7% for text gov_grants and 0.3% for the twin. The text-vs-twin RE drops by about 0.4% on gov_grants and much less on the GM over H. This works against text, so it is conservative for P1.
- **Coverage:** the change is second order, under 0.1 pp.
- **G4 as coded:** src/analysis.py:64-72 does not check RB at all, only coverage gaps and variance RB, so this cannot flip G4 there.
- **G4 as written in the protocol:** it is "abs(RB) <= 0.1 RRMSE OR within 2 MC SE", and a bias of 0.08 SE alone still passes the 0.1 RRMSE branch.

**Cost of the fix.** The fix is cheap: about 5 × N_ts × p × q multiply-adds per spec, around 0.3 GFLOP. The cost saving that D-6 cites to justify the shortcut is negligible.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In src/mc.py model_predict, replace the fold-averaged-coefficient population prediction with the average of the clipped fold predictions (the protocol's m̄). Keep this before the `if ratio:` rescaling so the ratio-to-amount conversion stays as is:

        # population predictions: average of the fold models' clipped predictions (protocol m̄)
        P = np.mean([np.clip(b0_ + F @ Bx_, lo, hi) for b0_, Bx_ in fits], 0)
        if ratio:
            P = P * xU[:, None]
        sumM[cols] = P.sum(0)
        if need_U:
            M_U[:, cols] = P

The nocf path is unchanged, since there is a single fit there. The same change also fixes the mcalm population column M_U. After the fix, remove the D-6 row from prereg/deviations.md. If the shortcut is kept instead, the D-6 row's impact text should say: "constraint total biased low by 0.4-2% on zero-inflated amounts; induces RB of about -0.02 to -0.16 SE per replicate (mean about -0.08 SE text, -0.05 SE twin on gov_grants), slightly against the text arm."

confirmed.title: Stage 3 TA-hist-own imputes 0 for take-all nonrespondents that were unavailable at D (contrib, prog_rev, salaries, employees), which gives a common bias of up to -33%
confirmed.failure_scenario: LAST_CYCLE maps y_contrib, y_prog_rev, y_salaries and y_employees to lag_contrib, lag_prog_rev, lag_salaries and lag_employees. build_population.apply_availability (lines 120-121) sets those to 0.0 for avail_t1 = 0. y_gov_grants, fundraising, officer_comp and volunteers use the unmasked oracle_lag_* columns, which hold the true TY2022 values, so the rule is applied inconsistently, and the NTEE10 trend factor in protocol section 7.2 is missing. On ne_pop_v2 with production_design(n = 1000), 86 of the 206 take-all units are unavailable at D and 84 of them file late. Under TA-late, ta_values (line 76) adds 0 for these units. Against the population totals that is -33.1% for y_prog_rev (6.5e10 of 1.97e11), -29.7% for y_salaries, -19.4% for y_employees, -6.6% for y_contrib and -4.8% for y_expenses. The bias is the same in every replicate and every estimator. It swamps the take-some MSE: RE and BRF between any two NR arms go to about 1 and coverage goes to about 0 for these y (contrib and prog_rev are in H_D). confirmed.suggested_fix: For the own last-cycle value use the unit's TY2022 return values, i.e. the pre-availability lags, as is already done for oracle_lag_*. Store them before apply_availability overwrites them (for example as last_* columns). Apply the protocol's NTEE10 trend ratio among responding take-all units, and use TA-hist-aux (lag_expenses x ratio) only where the own value is truly missing. Fix this before Stage 3 runs.

verdict.evidence:
I could not refute this finding. It is real, and every number in it checks out.

1) Code path. In src/stage34_ne.py, LAST_CYCLE (lines 31-36) maps y_employees, y_salaries, y_contrib and y_prog_rev to lag_employees, lag_salaries, lag_contrib and lag_prog_rev. In src/build_population.py, apply_availability (lines 115-121) sets those four columns to 0.0 wherever the TY2022 return was submitted after D. The same function sets lag_revenue and lag_expenses to bmf_revenue_amt, so for those units y_expenses is "imputed" with the BMF revenue amount. The oracle_lag_* columns (gov_grants, fundraising, officer_comp, volunteers) are never masked, so the rule is applied inconsistently. ta_values (line 76) returns Y[resp].sum + L[~resp].sum. run_cell (mc.py line 419) uses that as T_ta for every estimator in the replicate, so any error in it is common to all arms.

2) Check on /tmp/claude-0/data/pop/ne_pop_v2.parquet, single-threaded, using the production_design take-all rule (top 1% by lag_expenses):

confirmed.title: SAE twin and text arms get independent, unbalanced folds (shared-fold rule T4 broken in Stage 4)
confirmed.failure_scenario: run_sae never sets cell.fold_of, which stays at -1 from Cell.__init__, so model_predict always takes the fallback at mc.py:240, make_folds(len(i), 5, rng, groups), with no strata. A single generator rng = default_rng([seed, r, 7]) (sae.py:78) is passed first to the 'twin' model and then to the 'text' model, and the first call advances it. Reproduced: two consecutive make_folds calls on that generator put only 19.9% of 800 units in the same fold, which is chance. Each domain's text-vs-twin difference in MA_ and FH_ therefore includes independent fold noise from cross-fitting and from lambda CV, which widens or distorts the per-domain RE distribution. sae.parquet has already been produced this way.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In run_sae, set cell.fold_of[i] = make_folds(len(i), 5, default_rng([seed, r, 1]), grp, strata) once per replicate, before the models loop, as run_cell does. Keep the fallback for direct calls, but derive it from a per-replicate seed rather than a shared generator. Rerun Stage 4.

verdict.evidence:
The mechanism is confirmed. It breaks pre-registered rule T4 (protocol line 469: "one fold vector per replicate, seeded by (cell_seed, r, 1), is used by every arm (twin, text and controls) and by both λ-CV and cross-fitting", with folds dealt round-robin within design strata). Its effect, though, is limited to Monte Carlo precision. It adds no bias and does not touch any gate.

Code path:
(1) stage34_ne.sae() builds a fresh Cell, and Cell.__init__ (mc.py:222) sets fold_of = -1. run_sae (sae.py:60-128) never assigns cell.fold_of.
(2) model_predict therefore always takes the fallback at mc.py:239-240: make_folds(len(i), 5, rng, groups). It passes no strata, so groups are dealt into folds at random overall rather than within design strata.
(3) One generator, rng = default_rng([seed, r, 7]) at sae.py:78, is passed to "twin" and then to "text" at sae.py:97. make_folds is the only thing that draws from it, so twin's call advances it and text gets an independent partition. The B0 greg arm uses no rng.
Reproduced: two consecutive make_folds(800, 5, default_rng([20261023, 0, 7])) calls agree on 0.19875 of units, which is chance. sae.parquet (10:01) was written after the last edits to sae.py (09:45) and mc.py (09:42), so it was produced with this behaviour.

Size of the effect (4 real replicates, single-threaded, scratchpad fold_check.py). On the same sample, I used two different stratified fold vectors and compared the results with the 500-replicate spread in sae.parquet:
- For a single estimator, fold noise is a small share of its variance. For MA_text the median share is 0.2–5.5% depending on y (gov_grants 5.5%, contrib 2.6%, the rest under 1.5%).
- For the per-domain paired difference MA_text − MA_twin, fold noise matters much more. Independent folds give a median fold variance of 13–64% of the observed paired-difference variance. With shared folds the figure is 5–32%.

Why this does not refute the finding but limits it:
- Each estimator's fold assignment is uniformly random either way. Its marginal distribution, and so its expected per-domain MSE, does not depend on whether folds are shared. Per-domain RE (a ratio of MSEs in sae_metrics) is therefore unbiased.
- What changes is the correlation between the twin and text errors, which inflates the Monte Carlo noise of each per-domain RE. A rough estimate for gov_grants at R=500: the MC SD of log RE rises from about 2.0% to about 2.8%. That noise is far too small to move counts against thresholds such as "RRMSE +10%".
- The missing stratum balance applies equally to both arms.
- SAE output is not used by analysis.py, so no gate G1–G9 or primary pair is affected. The current sae.py is also not the protocol's S7 implementation (FH_frame/FH_text with frozen heads are marked [CODE]).

Verdict: a real but minor deviation that slightly widens the per-domain RE distribution. It cannot flip a gate.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In sae.run_sae, inside the replicate loop and right after s_ts and i are computed, add the following before the models loop:
    cell.fold_of[:] = -1
    grp_all = None if cell.groups is None else cell.groups[i]
    cell.fold_of[i] = make_folds(len(i), 5, np.random.default_rng([seed, r, 1]), grp_all, des.strata[s_ts])
(and import make_folds from mc). Twin and text then share one stratum-balanced, grouped fold vector, the same one run_cell would use for replicate r. Optionally, make mc.py:240 derive its fallback from a per-call seed instead of a caller-shared generator. Then rerun Stage 4 (stage34_ne.py sae 500), or log it as a deviation (T4 not applied in the Stage-4 pilot; it affects MC precision only, not expected RE).

confirmed.title: Fold groups cover only exact mission duplicates, and frozen training uses ungrouped folds
confirmed.failure_scenario: text_groups factorizes the normalized text_mission only, while protocol E4 and C4 (both blocking) require clusters with cosine > 0.95 and shared-URL groups. On E* (lsa256_full), 1,068 units have a cosine > 0.95 partner, and for 856 of them the partner is in a different fold group, so the pair can be split across folds. 1,256 units share a valid URL. frozen.train_frozen calls make_folds(len(r), 5, rng, None, hr) at frozen.py:93, i.e. with no groups, contrary to section 7.4 step 2 (grouped CV). Lambda selection, both in the MC and in the frozen heads, can therefore draw on near-duplicate text across folds. At f of about 5% few pairs are sampled together, so the expected shift is small, but control L6 is not actually implemented.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Build groups as the connected components of (exact mission) OR (cosine > 0.95 on E*) OR (same valid URL), and pass them to Cell and to train_frozen (groups=prev_groups[r]).

verdict.evidence:
I could not refute this finding. Every factual claim holds up, but the effect is very small and I don't think it changes any verdict or gate.

1. **Code matches the description.** `experiments.text_groups` (src/experiments.py:11-16) only factorizes the normalized `text_mission`. `stage2_ne.py:84` and `stage34_ne.py:67,109` pass only these groups to `Cell`. `frozen.train_frozen` calls `make_folds(len(r), 5, rng, None, hr)` at src/frozen.py:93, so its folds ignore even exact duplicates.

2. **The protocol requires more.** T4 (protocol line 469) requires grouping on exact duplicates, cosine > 0.95 clusters on E*, and shared valid URLs. A4 (line 1430), the `text_groups` extension (line 1511), A8 "grouped λ-CV" and §7.4 step 2 say the same. No grep hit for L6 or ungrouped folds anywhere in src/. None of D-1 to D-16 in deviations.md mentions fold grouping, so this is an undocumented deviation.

3. **The counts are confirmed.** I ran a single-threaded, chunked cosine check on `lsa256_full`, the embedding the `Cell` is built from:
   - 2,660 pairs have cosine > 0.95, and 1,635 of them fall in different exact groups.
   - 1,068 units have a partner, and 856 have a partner in a different group.
   - 1,503 of the split pairs are both take-some units.
   - By my own URL normalization, 1,373 units share a valid URL; 1,305 of them sit at URLs whose units span more than one exact group.

4. **Size of the effect per replicate.** In 20 simulated D1 draws (about 794 take-some units each):
   - 0 to 12 cosine pairs per draw (expected about 4.7) land in the sample split across groups.
   - 1 to 15 shared-URL pairs per draw with different exact groups are sampled together.
   - About 4/5 of these pairs end up in different folds.
   - In frozen training (about 410 respondents per head), I counted 5 to 62 exact-duplicate pairs in the full take-some sample (current-wave frame used as a proxy). Respondents are about half the sample, so roughly a quarter of those pairs survive, and about 4/5 of those are split.

   So the fold vectors, and hence λ and the cross-fitted residuals, do differ from the protocol's in most replicates. Estimates change, but only through a dozen or so of about 800 units.

5. **Why no verdict changes.**
   - This is a design-based Monte Carlo: RE comes from the true MC variance against the population total. Fold choice only changes the tuning, so ungrouped folds cannot fake a gain in G1/G2/G5. The only possible artificial optimism is a small downward bias in v_L from shrunken cross-fitted residuals, which affects coverage only.
   - Cross-fitting stays design-valid without groups, because the model for fold k does not use unit i's own inclusion.
   - FROZEN heads are fixed relative to the current sample, so ungrouped previous-wave CV only affects how good the heads are, not whether the estimator is unbiased or its variance valid.

**Bottom line:** a real but minor protocol deviation. The L6 control is not implemented and T4/§7.4 grouped CV is not honored. The expected effect on gates is negligible.
verdict.corrected_fix:
The R=2000 run already loaded this code and cached its frozen heads in prep.npz. So first log a deviation, D-17, in prereg/deviations.md before reading the Stage 2A results. It should say: folds grouped on exact mission only, frozen λ-CV ungrouped, expected effect a small change in λ and v_L, about 10 split pairs per replicate. Then, for later stages, replace text_groups with a union-find over three edges:

```python
def text_groups(pop, E=None, cos=0.95, url_col="website"):
    from scipy.sparse import coo_matrix
    from scipy.sparse.csgraph import connected_components
    N = len(pop)
    norm = (pop.text_mission.fillna("").str.lower()
            .str.replace(r"[^a-z ]", " ", regex=True)
            .str.replace(r"\s+", " ", regex=True).str.strip())
    r, c = [], []
    def link(codes):
        codes = np.asarray(codes); ok = codes >= 0
        idx = np.flatnonzero(ok)
        first = pd.Series(idx).groupby(codes[ok]).transform("first").to_numpy()
        r.extend(idx); c.extend(first)
    link(pd.factorize(norm)[0])
    if url_col in pop:
        w = (pop[url_col].fillna("").str.lower().str.strip()
             .str.replace(r"^(https?://)?(www\.)?", "", regex=True).str.rstrip("/"))
        valid = w.str.contains(r"\.") & ~w.isin(["n/a", "none", "na", "see schedule o"])
        link(pd.factorize(w.where(valid))[0])          # NaN -> -1, ignored
    if E is not None:
        En = E / (np.linalg.norm(E, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)
        for a in range(0, N, 2000):
            i, j = np.nonzero(En[a:a+2000] @ En.T > cos)
            r.extend(i + a); c.extend(j)
    G = coo_matrix((np.ones(len(r)), (r, c)), shape=(N, N))
    return connected_components(G, directed=False)[1]
```

- **Callers:** use `groups=text_groups(pop, Es)` in stage2_ne.py:84 and stage34_ne.py:67,109.
- **Frozen training:** in `train_frozen`, compute `pg = text_groups(prev, prev_E)` once and call `make_folds(len(r), 5, rng, pg[r], hr)` at frozen.py:93.
- **L6 control:** add it as a report-only rerun of the primary MCAL pair with `groups=None`.

The finding is partly real. Part (a) is refuted. Parts (b) and (c) are real gaps between the gate code and the protocol.

(a) N4 is refuted. pcs(np.ones) does return all-NaN columns (frame.py:65). Cell then drops them (mc.py:204, `np.abs(v).sum(0) > 0` is False for NaN). The same thing happens to the zero columns that a PCA of any constant embedding gives after centering. So any faithful version of the protocol's N4 ("every unit gets the same vector", passed through Z_K) gives the twin's matrix. The code matches the protocol here, not something narrower. The claim that "N4 cannot fail" is also false. Each estimator gets its own RNG stream, default_rng([seed, r, crc32(name)]) (mc.py:422), and private folds are the fallback when shared folds are missing (mc.py:238-240, 313). So the N4 arm would differ from the twin if fold sharing broke, or if anything in the code depended on the estimator's name. That is the failure the protocol names for N4 (§5.1: "Code-path or fold-sharing bug"). The mini output has a max abs difference of 0.0, as expected.

(b) G3 is real. So a placebo leak in the P2 single weight would not show in gates.csv. The verdict notebook (notebooks/03_protocol_stage2_ne_verdict.py:71) relies on that table alone. The 6-rep mini output shows placebo REs near 1 for these pairs, which tells nothing at R=6, so it is not yet known whether this changes a verdict.

(c) G4 is real and likely to matter. §9.2 has four G4 criteria. The code (analysis.py:69) checks three of them and leaves out "abs(RB) <= 0.1 x RRMSE or within 2 MC SE". Its var RB is relative to the empirical variance (analysis.py:32). §8.1 defines it relative to the MSE and lists the empirical-variance version only as an "also".

The bias criterion is not vacuous for this data. In the earlier R=500 NE runs (/tmp/claude-0/data/results/mc_ne_v1_n1000_metrics.csv and mc_ne_frozen_n1000_metrics.csv), it fails for many calibration arms, text arms included:
- y_revenue: abs(RB)/RRMSE 0.31-0.34, 7-8 MC SE
- y_prog_rev: about 0.19, about 4 MC SE
- y_fundraising_exp: 0.11-0.16

- GREG_size_cat+lsa256_full:add10 on y_contrib: ratio 0.101, var RB -7.4%
- MCAL_raw+lsa256_full on y_salaries: ratio 0.114, var RB -12.5%

At R=2000 the MC SE is half as large, so the "within 2 MC SE" escape is harder to use.

A bias of 0.316 x RRMSE means Var = 0.9 MSE. A variance estimator with an empirical-variance RB of -10% then has an MSE-based RB of -19%. So the definition alone can move an item across the ±15% line.

Concrete failure: take the P2 arm FROZEN_calm+E on some y in A with RB = 0.3 x RRMSE and mean v_hat close to Var(est). gates() reports G4 as passed, but the protocol fails it. confirmed.title: SAE twin and text models get different fold vectors in each replicate (T4 shared folds broken)
confirmed.failure_scenario: run_sae never sets cell.fold_of (a fresh Cell, all -1), so model_predict falls back to make_folds(len(i), 5, rng, groups) (mc.py 240). That fallback uses no strata balancing, and it draws from the one rng=default_rng([seed, r, 7]) that both models share. The twin call advances the generator, so the text model gets different folds; I confirmed the rng state differs at the two calls in reps 0 and 1. The FH_text vs FH_twin comparison (S7) therefore mixes fold noise into the paired difference, and the λ-CV is not stratum-balanced.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In run_sae, set cell.fold_of[:] = -1 and cell.fold_of[i] = make_folds(len(i), 5, default_rng([seed, r, 1]), grp, des.strata[s_ts]) once per replicate, before the model loop, as run_cell does.

verdict.evidence:
I could not refute this. The mechanism happens in the production SAE run, so the finding is real, but it is minor.

1. `stage34_ne.sae()` builds a fresh `Cell` and calls `run_sae` on it directly. `Cell.__init__` (`mc.py` line 222) sets `fold_of` to all -1. `run_sae` (`sae.py` lines 81-106) never writes `fold_of`. So in `model_predict`, `folds = cell.fold_of[i]` is all -1 and the fallback at `mc.py` lines 238-240 always runs: `make_folds(len(i), 5, rng, groups)`. That call gets no `strata` argument, so the folds are grouped but not dealt within strata.
2. `rng = np.random.default_rng([seed, r, 7])` is created once per replicate (`sae.py` line 83). The same object goes to every model in the loop: B0 is GREG and never draws from it, then twin (`FC@F1p`), then text (`FC@F1p+Estar`). Inside `model_predict`, the only consumer of `rng` is `make_folds`, which calls `rng.random(len(u))`. So the twin call moves the generator forward and the text call gets a different permutation.
3. A single-threaded synthetic check (n=100, a group of 10 near-duplicates, 4 strata) with the same seed tuple `[20261023, 0, 7]` showed this. Two successive fallback calls agree on only 15% of the fold labels. The fallback folds are unbalanced within strata, e.g. counts per fold of [1,3,3,5,13] in one stratum. The T4 call `make_folds(..., default_rng([seed, r, 1]), grp, strata)` gives exactly [5,5,5,5,5] in the ungrouped strata.

This breaks protocol rule T4 (`benchmark-protocol.md` line 469): one fold vector per replicate, seeded by (cell_seed, r, 1), shared by every arm and by both the λ-CV and the cross-fitting. `deviations.md` does not record it as a deviation. The protocol itself lists "shared seeds" as a pending change to `run_sae` (line 1514).

Effect on results: λ is chosen on different folds, and the cross-fitted `M_s` and fold-averaged `M_U` differ, so the text model's MA/SYN/FH domain estimates (and the twin's) are not what T4 would give. Text-vs-twin paired differences per replicate also pick up fold noise. Bias is not affected: each arm is still a valid estimator with its own random folds, so ARRMSE over replicates stays unbiased, just noisier. It also cannot flip any national gate G1-G9, because those come from `run_cell`, which sets shared folds correctly. S7 compares against FH_frame, which is still listed as [CODE] (not yet implemented) in the protocol. So this is minor, not verdict-changing, but it is a real violation of a pre-registered rule.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In `sae.py`, change the import to `from mc import model_predict, make_folds`. Then in `run_sae`, right after `i = cell.ts_index[s_ts]` and before the model loop, add:

    cell.fold_of[:] = -1
    grp_all = None if cell.groups is None else cell.groups[i]
    cell.fold_of[i] = make_folds(len(i), 5, np.random.default_rng([seed, r, 1]), grp_all, des.strata[s_ts])

These folds are the same ones `mc.run_cell` builds for replicate r: same seed tuple, same grouping, same stratum-balanced dealing. With them, `model_predict` never hits the private-fold fallback, and twin and text share one balanced fold vector per replicate.

confirmed.title: Grouped folds cover only exact normalized-mission duplicates (protocol T4), and frozen heads use ungrouped folds; neither is logged
confirmed.failure_scenario: T4 requires near-duplicate missions (cosine > 0.95 on E*) and units sharing a valid URL to share a fold. text_groups groups only exact normalized mission strings. On the NE frame, 1,635 pairs with cosine > 0.95 on lsa256_full (856 units) are in different groups, and 449 shared valid URLs span more than one group (1,373 units). A near-duplicate pair sampled into different folds leaks y into the other's out-of-fold prediction. That biases λ-CV toward lower penalties and shrinks residual variance for text arms only, an optimistic shift of the kind the L6 control is meant to measure. frozen.py line 93 calls make_folds(len(r), 5, rng, None, hr) with groups=None, but §7.4 says 'λ is chosen by grouped CV'. Separately, all 114 empty missions form one group. The expected per-sample effect is small, since few pairs fall in one sample.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Build groups as connected components of {exact mission, cosine > 0.95 on E*, shared valid URL}. Pass the previous-wave groups into train_frozen's make_folds. Map empty text to singleton groups. Log the change in deviations.md.

verdict.evidence:
I could not refute this. It is a real, unlogged departure from the pre-registered fold rule, and it does change fold vectors and therefore estimates. The effect is very small, and it is unlikely to change any gate verdict.

Code facts, checked:
- In src/experiments.py:11-16, text_groups only factorizes the normalized mission string, so only exact duplicates are grouped.
- The protocol asks for more in three places: T4 (benchmark-protocol.md:469) says "exact normalized-mission duplicates, cosine > 0.95 clusters on E*, and shared valid URLs share a fold"; A4 (line 1430) says "Groups = experiments.text_groups ∪ cosine > 0.95 clusters ∪ shared valid URLs"; and line 1511 says "text_groups extended (cosine clusters, shared URLs)".
- That grouping reaches every cell: stage2_ne.py:84 and stage34_ne.py:67/109 pass groups=text_groups(pop) into Cell, and mc.py:416-417 uses them for the shared per-replicate folds.
- src/frozen.py:93 calls make_folds(len(r), 5, rng, None, hr), so the frozen heads use ungrouped folds. A8 (line 1443) and §7.4 (line 787) both say "grouped λ-CV".
- None of D-1..D-16 in prereg/deviations.md covers either point.

Numbers, single-threaded on ne_pop_v2 and lsa256_full:
- 2,660 pairs have cosine > 0.95. Of these, 1,635 fall in different exact groups, covering 856 units. This matches the finding.
- 449 valid URLs span more than one exact group, covering about 1,305 units with my rough URL normalization (the finding says 1,373).
- Under the production design (n=1000, 794 take-some units), a sample is expected to contain about 4.7 cross-group cosine pairs and about 7.7 cross-group URL pairs.
- In 20 draws through make_folds, 0 to 14 cosine pairs appeared per sample, and about 85% of them were split across folds.
- Leakage matters because y is similar within these pairs: the correlation of log ratio y/x̃ across cosine pairs is 0.79 for y_gov_grants, 0.61 for volunteers and 0.31-0.34 for contrib/salaries.
- Still, about 10 leaky pairs out of 794 units is a tiny share. The resulting optimistic shift for text arms in λ-CV and cross-fitting is the kind L6 measures, and it is far too small to change G1-G9.

One part of the finding does not hold. The "114 empty missions form one group" point is not a defect: protocol E4 (line 1180) already accepts "largest cluster = empty mission (112)". In a sample only about 5 such units share one fold, so the round-robin balance barely moves.

Severity: minor. It is a real protocol/logging gap with a small optimistic bias for text arms, and it is unlikely to flip any gate.
verdict.corrected_fix: In experiments.text_groups, build connected components (union-find, or scipy.sparse.csgraph.connected_components) over three edge types: (a) the same normalized mission (non-empty), (b) cosine > 0.95 on the row-normalized E* (lsa256_full), computed in chunks, and (c) the same normalized valid URL, using the C3 rule: contains a dot, not N/A/NONE/NA/'see schedule o', with scheme, www and trailing slash stripped. Mapping empty missions to singletons is optional, since E4 accepts them as one cluster. In train_frozen, compute the same groups on the previous-wave frame using prev_E, then pass groups_prev[r] to make_folds(len(r), 5, rng, groups_prev[r], hr). Add a deviation entry to deviations.md if runs already done used exact-only groups; L6 (ungrouped) brackets the direction of the effect.

rejected.title: N4const control is a no-op: PCs of a constant embedding are 0/0 = NaN, and Cell silently drops the NaN columns, so the G2 N4 check is vacuous
rejected.why:
The mechanics in the finding are correct, but they do not change any estimate or any gate, and the finding misstates what N4 is meant to test.

What checks out: pcs(np.ones((N,D)),k) at src/frame.py:62-66 centres to an exactly zero matrix, so Z / Z.std(0) gives 0/0 = NaN, with the RuntimeWarning. Cell's rule `np.abs(v).sum(0) > 0` (src/mc.py:204-205) is False for NaN, so the 16 columns are dropped, and FC@F1p+N4const ends up as the same matrix as FC@F1p. In mini_stage2.parquet, MCAL_bmfmax@F1p+N4const minus MCAL_bmfmax@F1p has a max absolute difference of exactly 0.0.

Why it is not a defect:
(1) The suggested fix changes nothing. A constant embedding has centred PCs that are exactly zero in exact arithmetic. If pcs divided by np.where(sd>0, sd, 1), Z would be all-zero columns, and Cell drops all-zero columns by the same rule. I checked this on synthetic data: the keep mask is [T,T,T,F,F,F,F] for both the NaN block and the zero block. So every N4 estimate, and the G2 value of 0.0 <= 1e-8, is the same before and after the fix. Any implementation that follows the protocol's definition (benchmark-protocol.md:533, "Every unit gets the same vector") collapses to the twin. The protocol has no "zero-information continuous block" for RidgeGram to see; "constant-but-finite kept columns" would be a different control from the one pre-registered.
(2) The gate is not vacuous for its stated purpose. Protocol line 533 says N4 detects a "Code-path or fold-sharing bug". run_cell (src/mc.py:397-422) gives each estimator its own internal RNG, default_rng([seed, r, _stable_hash(name)]), so the twin and the +N4const spec get different streams. Suppose model_predict or cv_select stopped using the shared cell.fold_of and fell back to rng-drawn folds (mc.py:238-240). The two estimates would then differ even with identical matrices, and G2-N4 would fail. So the check still exercises fold sharing and determinism between two separately named specs.
(3) The constant-block invariance the finding wants covered (kept constant columns, same lambda path and Schur/eigen solve) is already tested on synthetic data in src/test_harness.py:54-63. That test appends np.ones((N,4)), which Cell keeps, and requires rel diff < 1e-8.

No estimator output, gate result or verdict depends on this. At most it is a cosmetic RuntimeWarning.

rejected.title: Bounded single-weight calibration: the non-convergence flag is discarded, and an all-bounded stratum yields NaN weights reported as converged
rejected.why:
The code does what the finding says, but the failure never happens on this benchmark's workload, so no estimate, failure count or gate changes.

1. **The code facts are correct.** `_calibrate_single` (src/mc.py:291-298) returns `conv`, and both callers drop it. FROZEN_calm at mc.py:326 and MCALm at mc.py:347 both do `t, e, g, conv = ...; return t, e`. `run_cell` (mc.py:431-433) counts only `LinAlgError` as a failure. The NaN mechanism in `bounded_calibration` (src/survey.py:225-249) is also real. I confirmed it on synthetic data: a dummy category with one sampled unit that needs g = 8 gets pinned at 5. The next solve divides by the 1e-310 ridge, and `0*inf` in `Xf @ lam` gives NaN for the other 199 weights. NaN fails both bound tests, so the function returns `(NaN weights, True)`.

2. **None of it can trigger here.** The algorithm only moves forward: every pass that does not return pins at least one more free unit, and pinned units sit exactly at L or U, so they never re-enter `out`.
   - **maxit = 50** needs at least 50 pinned units.
   - **`free.sum() <= p`** needs about 1000 - 59 pinned units.
   - **The NaN path** needs every sampled unit with some dummy = 1 to be pinned. The design has min_n = 10 per take-some stratum (frame.py:13, confirmed min n_h = 10). The other dummies (state, NTEE10, 1-avail) each cover hundreds to thousands of units. The stratum dummy also forces the d-weighted mean of g to 1 within each stratum.

3. **Exact replay of the running MC.** Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-hananather/61c19d0b-7d5d-50f6-9821-a76e0ea08cdb/scratchpad/bc_check.py, single-threaded, 23 s. It uses the same seed (20261023), the same `des.draw` order as `run_cell`, the same take-some restriction, `size_cat@F1p` (55 columns) plus the 4 J4 frozen heads, and the same `rep % 20` head cycling. Over all 2000 replicates, for both `FROZEN_calm_bmfmax@F1p+Estar` (P2 production) and `FROZEN_calm_bmfmax@F1p` (P2 twin):
   - 0 non-converged runs and 0 NaN weights.
   - Largest relative calibration error 7e-10.
   - Bound hits: mean 2.5, 99th percentile 11-12, maximum 26. That is well below the 50 needed for maxit and nowhere near a whole pinned stratum.

   The true failure rate is therefore 0%, so the §8.1 rule (over 0.5% flagged, over 2% excluded) and G1 come out the same whether or not `conv` is recorded.

4. **MCALm not fully replayed.** Replaying it costs a model fit per replicate, so I did not run 2000. Its arms show no NaN in the 6-replicate output (/tmp/claude-0/scripts/mini_stage2.parquet). It uses the same `X_base` and the same algorithm, so the counting argument applies. Even if a non-converged run did happen, the estimate would be a finite truncated-weight total, not a wrong value. A NaN would surface as NaN in `metrics`, not be silently absorbed.

What remains is a gap against protocol line 502 ("Non-convergence is flagged") in the diagnostics. It has no effect on any estimate or verdict.

rejected.title: Previous wave (P1') has no t-2 text fallback, so 8.7% of units (37% of revenue) are name-only in E* selection and frozen-head training, while the current wave gives them TY2021 text
rejected.why:
The facts in the finding are right, but the consequences it claims do not happen, and none of it is leakage.

Facts confirmed:
- /tmp/claude-0/data/pop/ne_wave2022_pop_v2.parquet has text_source {t-1: 18544, name: 1773}, and the name-only texts average 4.6 words. There is no TY2020 parse in data/parsed (only 2021, 2022 and 2023), so --prev2 could not have been used.
- The frozen embeddings were built from these texts. I recomputed the hashes: they match emb/ne_frozen/lsa256_full_prev.json and lsa256_full_curr.json.
- On scale: 1,687 of the name-only units are take-some. They hold 9-24% of the take-some totals of the H targets (18.6% of take-some revenue). The 37% revenue figure covers all units, and most of the gap is 86 take-all units, which the ceilings and frozen training both exclude.

1. Not a protocol violation and not a leak.
- The text rule in §2.2, "TY2022, else TY2021, else name", is written for the current wave only. §2.6, §6.5 and §7.4 set no TY2020 text fallback for P1'; B5 is the only rule they impose on P1', and frozen.py and stage1_select.py both apply it.
- Name-only text gives the previous wave less information, not more, so there is no leak.
- The related problem, BMF amounts dated after D', is already logged in protocol §12.4 ("Previous-wave codes from a BMF (2023-08) that post-dates D′ … Slightly favourable to frozen heads"). The finding itself calls it negligible.

2. Claim (a), that the E* selection would change, is refuted.
- I reran the Stage-1 selection exactly as /tmp/claude-0/scripts/stage1_select.py does it (_b5, FC@F1p, ceiling_av, pcs). The baseline reproduces the published numbers exactly: LSA full K = 16 / 32 / 64 = 1.0227 / 1.0333 / 1.0404.
- For the check, I gave the 1,773 name-only units their real TY2021 text (from ne_wave2022_pop.parquet) and refitted LSA. This gives them more information than TY2020 text would, so it bounds the fix from above.
- Results with that text: LSA full 1.0266 / 1.0320 / 1.0394; LSA mission at most 1.0067; MiniLM full at most 1.0207; MiniLM mission at most 1.0095.
- The best ceiling is 1.0394, so the tie window starts at 1.0194. LSA full K = 16 (1.0266) still wins, and its margin grows: the gap to the best shrinks from 0.0177 to 0.0128.
- E* is the same in both runs, so the P1 primary (which uses only E* on the current wave) is unaffected.

3. Claim (b), the frozen heads, has a negligible effect in the conservative direction.
- Only 413 of 12,085 previous-wave take-some respondents (3.4%) are name-only, about 20 per training sample.
- I ran train_frozen with the same seed and J = 20 on the baseline text and on the corrected text (LSA refitted). The twin heads are identical.
- I scored each head by the current-wave population anticipated variance of the difference estimator, then took the geometric mean over all 15 real targets of AV(twin)/AV(text). It moves from 1.0298 (baseline) to 1.0335 (corrected), about +0.4%.
- So the current build slightly understates the text heads for P2. It cannot inflate a text gain, and frozen heads stay design-unbiased either way. A 0.4% shift is within Monte Carlo noise, so it does not change P2 or any gate.

Conclusion: an undocumented asymmetry in the information sets. It has no effect on E*, a 0.4% conservative effect on the frozen heads, and no change to any verdict or gate. At most it deserves a one-line note in the deviations log.

rejected.title: The 'binding saving' in the real-world translation is the worst per-y 1-1/RE over H, not the protocol's binding-constraint saving
rejected.why:
This finding doesn't hold up as a defect. It cannot change any estimate, gate or verdict, and where it differs from the protocol it understates the saving rather than overstating it.

1. **Nothing downstream uses the number.** In /home/user/hananather/_research/embedding-auxiliary-variables/notebooks/03_protocol_stage2_ne_verdict.py, line 169 is a single `print`, and line 170 writes a CSV. Searching the repo for `real_world_translation` and `take-some saving` finds no other uses. No code checks the SUPPORTED rule: analysis.py only calls `protocol.verdict(pt, lo, hi)`, which applies the MET/OPEN/EXCLUDED and any-gain bars. SUPPORTED also needs P1 and P2 to pass the confirmatory test in 8 held-out divisions. The notebook itself says NE is the development, proof-of-concept population and that generalization is "not assessed here". So "the SUPPORTED rule would be judged on the wrong quantity" never happens.

2. **The protocol's own rule licenses the approximation, and the gap is declared.** Protocol §12.1 says σ ≈ 1 − 1/RE_binding (1.2 → 17%) and "RE r saves 1 − 1/r of the take-some sample, only for the binding variable". The notebook's markdown repeats this, and the print is plainly labelled "binding saving over H (minimum)". Deviation D-12 in prereg/deviations.md records that the multi-n cost-curve stages, which the §8.7 minimum-n calculation needs, were not run.

3. **The direction is conservative.** Without the fpc, n_T,y ≈ n_B,y/RE_y. The protocol's saving is 1 − max_y(n_B,y/RE_y)/max_y n_B,y, which is at least min_y(1 − 1/RE_y) over the targeted y. Taking the minimum over all of H, including prog_rev and officer_comp, which have no target, can only lower it further. §8.7 warns against the *best* single-y RE, which is the optimistic error; the notebook uses the *worst*, the opposite. I checked this on the 6-replicate mini output, using P2 (`FROZEN_calm_bmfmax@F1p+Estar`) against `GREG_size_cat@F1p`:

| y | RE | 1 − 1/RE |
|---|---|---|
| gov_grants | 1.348 | 25.8% |
| contrib | 1.518 | 34.1% |
| fundraising | 1.839 | 45.6% |
| volunteers | 0.996 | −0.4% |
| prog_rev | 0.838 | −19.3% |

So the printed −19.3% understates the saving. If anything this pushes toward a null, never toward a false SUPPORTED.

4. **The fpc effect is negligible.** Leaving out the fpc overstates the saving by about 0.6 percentage points at RE 1.2 (16.7% vs 16.1%). The protocol's own §12.1 rule leaves it out too.

The most that can be said is that the label "binding" is loose for a descriptive number. That is not a defect that changes any result.
